findings.checklist_item: - [ ] AC4: state the default fail-mode — prefer fail-closed (refuse to sign) with an explicit override, or justify warn-only — rather than leaving the choice to the executor.
evidence: "AC4: Signing refuses, or emits an explicit warning, when the environment cannot verify its own signatures"
signal (6) ambiguous priority: two viable behaviors with no ranking
the choice affects whether existing sign flows break (refuse) or proceed (warn)
findings.finding: AC4 leaves the fail-mode as an unranked either/or ('refuses, or emits an explicit warning') — fail-closed (refuse to sign) vs fail-open-with-warning are materially different behaviors that change the contract for every caller of sign_manifest.
scenarios: Executor picks 'warn only' and certificates that prove nothing continue to be minted, contradicting the plan's stated goal that 'a certificate that can never be certified must not be minted silently'
findings.suggested_fix: Rank AC4: default to refusing to sign when the environment has no usable public key, and require an explicit opt-in flag if a warn-and-proceed mode is needed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] AC2: pick a provisioning strategy — prefer deriving the public key from REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY at startup so it cannot drift, or state why a separately-shipped .pub is required.
evidence: "AC2: The deployment materializes the public key half wherever _opcert_own_public_key reads it, derived from or shipped alongside REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY"
signal (1)/(2): the source/provenance of the materialized public key is left to executor investigation
findings.finding: AC2 offers two provisioning strategies ('derived from or shipped alongside REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY') without picking one — deriving the ed25519 public key from the private key vs. shipping a separate .pub via secrets/mount are different deploy changes with different failure surfaces.
scenarios: Executor ships a separate .pub secret that can drift from the private key, reintroducing mismatch on the next re-clone that AC5 is meant to fix
findings.suggested_fix: Default to deriving the ed25519 public half from the private key at process start and writing it where _opcert_own_public_key reads, eliminating a separately-managed .pub that can drift.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the Mechanism/AC2 description with _opcert_own_public_key's re-derivation branch (lines 251-257): state that verify self-heals from a private key at <tracker>/.opcert-key, and that the failure is the path divergence between the /run/secrets signing mount and the tracker key path — not merely 'only the private key is supplied'.
evidence: Plan Mechanism: '_opcert_own_public_key reads the public key from the TRACKER directory'
_opcert_signing.py:251-257: 'if os.path.exists(key_path): _derive_opcert_pub(key_path)' — re-derives the .pub from a tracker-local private key when the .pub is absent
opcert_key_path() returns '<tracker>/.opcert-key' (line 57-59), NOT the REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY mount path
mcp_server.py:717-746 compose_startup_opcert_binding signs using cfg.identity.signing_key (the /run/secrets mount), a different path than the verify self-heal reads
findings.finding: The Mechanism section describes _opcert_own_public_key as reading the .pub from the tracker and returning None when absent, but the actual implementation re-derives the .pub from a private key when one exists at the tracker path (<tracker>/.opcert-key). The plan omits this self-healing branch, so the stated root cause is incomplete: verification fails not merely because 'the deployment supplies only the private key' but because that private key is at the /run/secrets mount (used by the SIGNING path via compose_startup_opcert_binding/REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY) whereas the VERIFY self-heal looks for a private key at <tracker>/.opcert-key, where none exists.
scenarios: Author designs AC2 fix to 'ship a .pub alongside the key' but the verify path already self-heals from a tracker-local private key, so the actual fix must reconcile the mount path vs. the tracker .opcert-key path divergence

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Mechanism to name the real edit seam: _opcert_own_public_key reads the tracker-relative <tracker>/.opcert-key(.pub), NOT the REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH/REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY mount that signing uses; the fix must reconcile these two paths (or teach the verify seam to consult the same override).
evidence: _opcert_signing.py:243 own_pub reads opcert_key_path(tracker) = '<tracker>/.opcert-key' (+ '.pub'), then re-derives from the tracker-relative private key at lines 251-257
_opcert_signing.py:189 signing reads override = os.environ.get('REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH') — a DIFFERENT path than the verify-side tracker-relative lookup
docker-compose.yml:285 REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH=/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key; the private key is NOT at <tracker>/.opcert-key
Plan claims: 'the deployment supplies only the PRIVATE key, via REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY, from a mount that has no public half' — but the verify seam does not read that mount at all
findings.finding: The Mechanism section mislocates the root cause: it attributes the foreign_key verdict to the mount lacking a public half, but the true asymmetry is a path mismatch. Signing resolves the private key via the REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH/REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY env override (_opcert_signing.py:189 -> /run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key), whereas _opcert_own_public_key reads <tracker>/.opcert-key.pub and re-derives from <tracker>/.opcert-key (_opcert_signing.py:243-257) — a tracker-relative lookup that never consults the env override. Because the private key lives only at the mount and NOT at <tracker>/.opcert-key, the re-derivation branch cannot fire either.
scenarios: A fix that ships a .pub alongside /run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key still yields foreign_key because _opcert_own_public_key never reads that directory
The plan's re-derivation claim (AC2 'derived from ... REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY') implies the code re-derives from the mount, but re-derivation is tracker-relative and cannot see the mount

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Mechanism/AC2 diagnosis to state that the verify reader sources the .pub from the TRACKER dir while the signer sources the private key from the REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY mount, and require the fix to materialize the .pub DERIVED FROM THE SAME MOUNTED SIGNING KEY the startup binding uses (not a fresh tracker-local keypair) so the public half provably matches the signing key.
evidence: _opcert_own_public_key reads `<tracker>/.opcert-key.pub` and re-derives from `<tracker>/.opcert-key` only if that private key is present (src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:243-258)

The signing path composes the signer from the mount: `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` -> compose_signer copies the key into a process-owned runtime dir (mcp_server.py:717-746; opcert_service/keyprov.py:62-95)
Plan quote: 'The re-clone regenerated .env-id but never restored .opcert-key.pub' — omits that the tracker also lacks the private key, so verify and sign draw from two different sources
findings.finding: The Mechanism section mis-diagnoses the source of the missing public key: the verify reader `_opcert_own_public_key` sources the `.pub` (and its re-derivation) from the TRACKER directory `<tracker>/.opcert-key[.pub]`, but the signing key is supplied at a DIFFERENT location (the `/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key` mount via `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`, copied into a process-owned runtime dir by the startup binding). The tracker holds neither the `.pub` nor the private key, so the reader's existing re-derive-from-private-key fallback cannot help. The plan frames the defect as 'the re-clone never restored .opcert-key.pub', which risks steering an implementer to regenerate a tracker-local keypair that would NOT match the mounted signing key and would still verify as foreign_key.
scenarios: Implementer regenerates a fresh keypair inside the tracker dir to satisfy AC2; the new .pub does not match the mounted signing key; verify_signature still returns foreign_key / invalid.
Implementer relies on the existing re-derive fallback, expecting a tracker-local private key that is not there.
findings.suggested_fix: In AC2, specify: 'derive `<tracker>/.opcert-key.pub` (or whatever path `_opcert_own_public_key` reads) via `ssh-keygen -y -f <REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY>` so the materialized public key is provably the counterpart of the mounted signing key', and add a note in Mechanism that the tracker holds neither key half in the observed deployment.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reframe AC2 to reuse the existing public-key derivation (`_derive_opcert_pub`/`_opcert_own_public_key` re-derivation) against the provisioned private-key path, rather than adding a new materialization mechanism — the 'derived from private key' capability already exists; the gap is where the verifier looks.
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:238-258 `_opcert_own_public_key`: 'if the .pub is missing but the private key is present, re-derive the public key' — then calls `_derive_opcert_pub(key_path)'
src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:62-94 `_derive_opcert_pub`/`_ensure_opcert_pub` already (re)derive `<key_path>.pub` via `ssh-keygen -y`
Plan mechanism section: signing key at /run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key while `_opcert_own_public_key` reads the tracker dir — a path mismatch, not missing derivation logic
findings.finding: AC2 proposes materializing the public key 'derived from or shipped alongside REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY', but the codebase already derives the public half from the private key on demand (`_derive_opcert_pub` via `ssh-keygen -y`, called by `_opcert_own_public_key` and `_ensure_opcert_pub` when `.pub` is absent). The actual gap is a LOCATION mismatch (private key at /run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key vs `_opcert_own_public_key` reading `<tracker>/.opcert-key.pub`), not absent derivation. Without steering the fix onto the existing derivation path, AC2 invites a parallel re-implementation (NIH).
scenarios: Implementer writes new key-materialization code when pointing `_opcert_own_public_key` at the provisioned private-key path (so its existing re-derivation fires) would suffice
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite AC2 as: 'Verification derives the public key from the provisioned private key wherever REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY points, by having `_opcert_own_public_key` consult the bound/provisioned key path (reusing `_derive_opcert_pub`) instead of only the tracker dir.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify in AC5 whether the re-clone path RESTORES the original key (preserving prior signatures) or REGENERATES a new one, and if regeneration is allowed, define what happens to attestations already signed under the old key (migration, re-sign, or explicit invalidation).
evidence: AC5: 'restores or regenerates the git-ignored local state it destroys (.opcert-key, .opcert-key.pub, .env-id)'
The key pair + .env-id are shared state consumed by every verify_signature call; regenerating a fresh keypair changes the principal/verification basis
Plan notes 'the audit trail silently records certificates' — old certs signed under a prior key would still exist
findings.finding: AC5 allows the re-clone path to 'restore OR regenerate' the git-ignored key state (.opcert-key, .opcert-key.pub, .env-id), but does not address the shared-state lifecycle consequence of regeneration: minting a NEW keypair leaves all previously-signed op-certs uncertifiable under the new public key, and the plan does not enumerate consumers of the old key or a retire/migration path for pre-existing signatures.
scenarios: Re-clone regenerates a fresh keypair; previously-minted completion-verifier attestations now verify as foreign_key against the new key, silently invalidating the historical audit trail
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer restoring .opcert-key/.opcert-key.pub/.env-id from a durable source on re-clone; only regenerate as a last resort, and if so, document that prior certs become uncertifiable and how the audit trail reflects that.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] For AC5/AC6/DD3, state whether the fix extends the existing mechanisms (`env_identity.CARRY_OVER`, fsck `ENV_ID_MISMATCH`, `compose_startup_opcert_binding` fail-closed) or introduces new ones, and justify any new surface.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py:66-88 `CARRY_OVER` already lists .env-id, .opcert-key, .opcert-key.pub, .ensure-applied with per-file breakage
src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py:13,52 ENV_ID_MISMATCH already a counted issue naming the dropped git-ignored state
src/rebar/mcp_server.py:732-735 `compose_startup_opcert_binding` already fail-closed: 'when both inputs are present but the key is invalid ... compose_signer raises and startup aborts'
Plan itself notes 'the diagnostic already exists; nothing acts on it'
findings.finding: AC5 and AC6 (restore git-ignored local state on re-clone; add a startup/deploy health check) may duplicate existing mechanisms. The codebase already enumerates the carry-over state (`env_identity.CARRY_OVER`: .env-id, .opcert-key, .opcert-key.pub, .ensure-applied), fsck already emits ENV_ID_MISMATCH for exactly this failure mode, and `compose_startup_opcert_binding` is already fail-closed on an invalid/missing key. The plan should confirm whether these existing surfaces are extended rather than a new restoration/health mechanism built alongside them.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria / AC5, AC6; Definition of Done / DD3
scenarios: Implementer adds a new health-check module when the existing fsck ENV_ID_MISMATCH / startup fail-closed path could be extended to also assert public-key usability

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how AC4's signing-refusal behavior reaches the deployed server (flag/canary vs. 100% flip) and a cheap rollback (e.g. warn-only mode toggle) so a false 'cannot verify' detection cannot block all closes with no undo.
evidence: AC4: 'Signing refuses, or emits an explicit warning, when the environment cannot verify its own signatures'
The close path currently returns "completion_signature": {"signed": true} — if signing begins refusing, closes on the deployed server change behavior immediately
No flag, canary, or rollback path is described for the refuse-on-close behavior
findings.finding: AC4 introduces a behavior change to the deployed server's signing path (signing may now REFUSE when the environment cannot verify itself), but the plan specifies no staged rollout or rollback for this change — a bad detection could cause the close path to start refusing to sign on 100% of traffic with no flag or quick undo.
scenarios: A misfiring 'cannot verify' check causes the deployed MCP server to refuse signing on every close, blocking ticket closure with no fast toggle to restore prior behavior
findings.suggested_fix: Default AC4 to warn-only, gate the hard-refuse behind an env flag, and document how to flip it back; note it in the enforcement-flip runbook.

findings.finding: The fix-side ACs (AC2 deployment materialization, AC5 re-clone restoration, AC6 startup/deploy health check) name no concrete edit targets, yet the in-repo consumers they must change are identifiable: infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh (materializes the private key with no .pub, lines 172-185), infra/compose/docker-compose.yml (the key bind-mounts), infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh (the re-clone path, lines 155-284), and infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh.
scenarios: Author implements AC2 by writing a .pub next to the mount but never touches the tracker-relative path _opcert_own_public_key actually reads
